newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-U.S. AND CZECHS JOIN SWEDEN IN MEDALS HUNT.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-U.S. AND CZECHS JOIN SWEDEN IN MEDALS HUNT.

text.p: The United States and the Czech Republic both won their third straight games at the world ice hockey championship on Wednesday to join Sweden in the final series.
Three more teams will go through next week from the two preliminary round-robin pools.
In pool B in Turku, Canada suffered a surprise setback by drawing 3-3 with lowly Latvia.
In pool A in Helsinki, Russia scored a 5-4 victory over France to stay in contention for a place in the final series.
The United States struck three third-period goals to beat Italy 4-2 and keep their 100 percent record in pool B.
The victory left the Americans, who are seeking their first world title in 64 years, with a perfect record of 3-0 and lifted them to joint first place with Sweden.
Calgary Flames' Marty McInnis collected the winner midway through the final period when he snapped a point-blank wrist-shot past Italian netminder Mike Rosati.
Canada also needed third-period goals to earn their draw against Latvia.

Jarome Iginla's goal with less than five minutes remaining allowed Canada to escape with the draw and prevented Latvia from claiming their first world championship win in 58 years. Canada had trailed 3-1 going into the final period.
The result leaves Canada in third place in pool B on three points, three behind Sweden and the United States.

Mark Recchi, who joined the team on Monday after the Montreal Canadiens were eliminated from the Stanley Cup playoffs, pulled Canada to within one before Ignila batted a slapshot past Latvian netminder Juris Klodans to get the draw.
In pool A, Czech goalkeeper Roman Chechmanek made 33 saves to keep his team afloat against neighbours Slovakia.
The Slovaks, who have never beaten the Czechs, had more of the game but were denied by Chechmanek's phenomenal saves.

Leading 2-1 and under fierce attack, Czech forward Vladimir Vujtek received a long pass from Libor Prochazka, advanced on the right and scored the goal which put the outcome beyond doubt with just 59 seconds left of the game.
The Czechs remained the only team in group A not having dropped a single point. Slovak head coach Jozef Golonka said his side had defeated itself and were now unlikely to reach the medal games.

Russia kept alive their hopes of reaching the final stages with a late goal by Alexander Barkov for their narrow win against France. After the first half of the match, Russia seemed headed for an easy victory, leading 4-0.
But France refused to cave in and their team spirit soared as Roger Dube and Pierre Allard, assisted by Dube, scored two goals inside 74 seconds halfway into the second period.
The French comeback mercilessly highlighted the chief weaknesses of the Russian side - the lack of a reliable goalkeeper, and non existent teamwork when the going gets tough.
Four minutes before the end, Arnaud Briand equalised, but Barkov restored order just 21 seconds later. He coolly waited out French goaltender Francois Gravel and whipped the puck into the net.
Russia, on five points, and Finland with four look the likely teams to join the Czechs in the medals hunt, although Slovakia may yet fininsh among the top three in group A.

France, with three straight losses, are certain to travel to Tampere for the relegation play-offs after the preliminary round-robin groups. Germany and Norway are also out of the running for the final series.
